site_description: Play Briscola against bots and watch how they think.
home_lead: Play Briscola against bots and watch how they think: the hands they imagine, the cards they weigh, the score they expect.

privacy_body: The site uses Umami, on our own server, to count page views and finished games. Umami sets no cookies and stores no IP addresses or other data that identify a person.
privacy_event: At the end of a game the site sends one event with the bot, the engine version, the level, who won, the point difference and whether you looked at the bot's cards. The moves are not sent.

credits_cards_body: The cards are the Naples deck on Wikimedia Commons, by Trocche100, in the public domain. We cleaned off the printer's marks. Here is every file with its source.
lab_caption_ratings: Bradley-Terry ratings from the round robin, {deals} duplicate deals per pair. The champion in orange.
lab_caption_versus: Each bot's score against {champion}, with the 95% interval. A hollow dot means the interval includes 50%: the two bots cannot be told apart.
lab_caption_matrix: The row's score against the column, in percent. Blue: the row wins, its 95% interval above 50%. Orange border: they cannot be told apart.
home_watch_body: Pick two bots and watch them play each other, card by card, with both bots' reasoning.
credits_bots_body: The bots' robots are generated with DiceBear's Bottts style, free for personal and commercial use:
settings_note: Your choices stay in this browser and are not sent anywhere.
settings_sound_body: The shuffle, the cards dealt, played and gathered, and the end of the game. They start from the first tap on the page.
rules_lead: Briscola for two: 40 cards, three in hand, 120 points in all. Whoever takes more than 60 wins.
rules_deck_body: Forty Neapolitan cards in four suits: coppe, denari, bastoni and spade. Each suit runs from the Ace to the King.
rules_points_body: Five cards in each suit are worth points. The Ace and the Three are called carichi; the cards worth nothing are called lisci.
rules_points_order: The order of points is also the order of strength: the Ace beats the Three, the Three beats the King, and so on down to the Two.
rules_briscola_body: The dealer gives three cards to each player, then turns the next card face up and puts it under the deck. Its suit is the briscola for the whole game, and that card is the last one drawn.
rules_briscola_caption: The deck, with the Seven of coppe face up: the briscola is coppe.
rules_trick_body: The leader plays a card; the other player answers with any card. There is no need to follow suit or to play a briscola.
rules_trick_hint: In the examples the briscola is coppe. Tap “Who takes it?” for the answer.
rules_example_suit: Same suit: the stronger card wins. The Three beats the King.
rules_example_other: Another suit never wins, not even with the Ace. The Seven of denari takes 11 points.
rules_example_briscola: A briscola beats any card of another suit: the Two of coppe takes the Ace of spade.
rules_example_both: Between two briscole the stronger wins: the Three takes the King.
rules_draw_1: The winner gathers both cards and keeps them face down.
rules_draw_2: The winner draws first, then the other player. Both are back to three cards.
rules_draw_3: The winner leads the next trick.
rules_draw_4: On the last draw one face-down card and the briscola are left: the winner draws the face-down card, the other player the briscola. The last three cards are played without drawing.
rules_end_body: At the end each player counts the points in the cards they took.
rules_end_settled: As soon as someone passes 60 points the game is settled: the tricks left cannot change the result. Here the game ends at that moment.
rules_tip_1: When you cannot take the trick, answer with a liscio, so you give away no points.
rules_tip_2: Don't spend a briscola on two lisci: keep it for the carichi.
rules_tip_3: Count the briscole played. Knowing where the Ace of briscola is changes the game.
network_caption: It plays the most likely card. Neurons: the {shown} most active of {width} per layer.
